Site table of a profile

Source: R/accessors.R
site_table.Rd

Returns one row for each site: its estimate and standard error, its reliability, its term of the dispersion \(H\), its proportion of the total reliability, and, when the estimates are known, the posterior mean and standard deviation of its effect.

Usage

site_table(x, level = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

An object of class reliability_profile, reliability_posterior, reliability_draws or reliability_design.

level

Probability content of the posterior intervals, a number between 0 and 1. NULL, the default, uses the level of the fit. Not used for a profile at a fixed between-site SD.

...

Must be empty.

Value

A data frame with one row per site and the columns

  • site, estimate (when known) and se.

  • for a design, n, kappa and n_balanced: the planned size, the variance constant and the size under balance or equal spending.

  • reliability: the site's reliability, its posterior mean for a posterior fit or draws, which also have reliability_lower and reliability_upper, the ends of its posterior interval.

  • kl_term: the site's term of \(H\); share: its proportion of the total reliability.

  • when the estimates are known, effect and effect_sd: the posterior mean and standard deviation of the site's effect, and for a posterior fit or draws effect_lower and effect_upper, the ends of its posterior interval.

Details

For a profile at a fixed sigma_tau, the effect's posterior mean and standard deviation are those of the normal model at that sigma_tau, with a flat prior on the mean of the effects: \(S_j \hat\tau_j + (1 - S_j)\hat\mu\) and \(\{\sigma_\tau^2(1 - S_j) + (1 - S_j)^2 / W\}^{1/2}\), where \(\hat\mu\) is the precision-weighted mean of the estimates with weights \(w_j = 1/(\sigma_\tau^2 + v_j)\) and \(W = \sum_j w_j\). A profile inherited from a fitted mean model uses the site's fitted value \(x_j'\hat\beta\) in place of the common mean, and \(x_j'(X'\Omega X)^{-1}x_j\) in place of \(1/W\), where \(\Omega\) is the diagonal matrix of the weights \(w_j\).

The column share is the proportion of the total reliability at site \(j\), \(S_j / \sum_k S_k\). At a fixed sigma_tau the inverse of the sum of the squared proportions is the concentration count. For a posterior fit the columns are posterior means, and that identity is only approximate.

See also

profile_summary() for the diagnostics, and plot_pooling() and plot_profile() for plots of the sites.

Examples

prof <- reliability_profile(se = c(0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30), sigma_tau = 0.2,
                            estimate = c(0.3, 0.1, -0.1, 0.5))
site_table(prof)
#>   site estimate   se reliability     kl_term     share     effect  effect_sd
#> 1    1      0.3 0.10   0.8000000 0.134361601 0.3559206 0.27629021 0.09333724
#> 2    2      0.1 0.15   0.6400000 0.009963631 0.2847365 0.12932238 0.12925311
#> 3    3     -0.1 0.20   0.5000000 0.010239076 0.2224504 0.04072553 0.15636178
#> 4    4      0.5 0.30   0.3076923 0.148205370 0.1368925 0.27946612 0.19032017
